newsitem.title: INDIA: PRESS DIGEST - Indian newspapers - May 28.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Indian newspapers - May 28.

text.p: Following is a summary of major Indian business and political stories in leading newspapers prepared for REUTERS by Business News and Information Services Pvt Ltd, New Delhi Tel:3326806, 3326813, 3326849 Fax:+91-11-3351006 E-mail: biznis@giasdl01.vsnl.net.in
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
TOP STORIES
The Hindustan Times
PAWAR DECIDES TO CONTEST AGAINST KESRI

Former federal minister Sharad Pawar decided to enter the contest for the post of Congress party president. He will be filing his nomination paper on the last date, May 28. Pawar took the decision after consulting several senior Congress leaders. He had met Sonia Gandhi on Monday. His decision hots up the race for the top post in the All India Congress Committee, making this year's poll one of the most keenly contested organisational elections witnessed by the Congress in the last 20 years. Pawar's move might be a setback for the current incumbent, Sitaram Kesri, who thought he would have to face only a token resistance from Rajesh Pilot.
The Economic Times
COGENTERIX SURVEY DISRUPTED

A 500-strong mob disrupted an engineering survey being carried out by the Mangalore Power Company to mark the boundary of the 1,000 mw Cogentrix thermal power project near Mangalore. They also gathered in front of the office of the U.S.' power company this morning and raised slogans against the project. No untoward incident was reported and the situation was peaceful. An environmental activist, who was at the spot, said people pelted the company's office with stones. But the police denied this. The protesters have threatened to intensify the agitation if the company does not stop work immediately. The survey was completed by this afternoon.
RBI RECALLS APPROVAL FOR COX & KINGS' BANK

The Reserve Bank (RBI) recalled its in-principle approval granted to Cox & Kings to set up a bank. An RBI spokesperson said the approval was withdrawn after the company failed to show any progress in setting up a bank. The RBI is believed to have sent a letter to the company recalling the approval.
CRB OFFICE SEALED IN DELHI

The official liquidator of the Delhi High Court has sealed the office of CRB Capital Markets, which is alleged to be involved in financial irregularities worth hundreds of millions of rupees being investigated by federal police and the central bank.
RUSH TO OFFER $100 MLN EUROBONDS

Several Indian corporates have lined up $100-million fixed rate Eurobond offerings with 10 year maturities. The Steel Authority of India (SAIL) is already in the market with a $100 million 10-year maturity offer. Other companies in the fray include Telco, Larsen & Toubro, BSES, Hindalco and Indian Petro-chemicals Corp. All the companies are hoping to take advantage of recent relaxations in external commercial borrowing guidelines. The new guidelines say there would not be any end-use restrictions on companies raising funds up to $100 million and with 10-year maturities.
Financial Express
SUB-BROKERS TO SEEK EXTENSION OF DEADLINE

Sub-brokers of Bombay Stock Exchange (BSE) members will be requesting the Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI) to extend the deadline of June 1 for registration of sub-brokers to July 31. The reason given is that a revised format of the member -sub-broker agreement has reached them only on May 23.
ZURICH INSURANCE TO INCREASE STAKE IN 20TH CENTURY FUND

20th Century Finance has decided to reduce its stake in Centurion Mutual Fund from 57 percent to 26 percent in favour of Switzerland-based Zurich Insurance Corporation. Zurich Insurance Corporation which already holds a majority stake of 33 percent, will be pumping in $5 million to increase its stake in Centurion Asset Management Company (AMC) to 64 percent. The Swiss insurance giant holds a stake in the AMC through Kemper Corporation of US, which was taken over by the former. The 10 percent stake in the AMC held by the International Finance Corporation will remain the same.
TIME-FRAME ON SERVICE TAX FOR BROKERS EASED
The Central Board of Excise and Customs (CBEC) has relaxed the time-frame to pay service tax on brokerage from 30 days to 75 days. The new rule is effective from June 1.
Business Standard
INSURANCE FIRMS MAY INVEST IN PRIVATE COMPANIES

Insurance companies have been allowed to invest in both private sector equity and debt without obtaining government's approval. The decision was obviously taken with a view to pep up capital market sentiments. But such investments will remain subject to prudential norms. The Life Insurance Corporation will have to abide by the norm of investing at least 75 percent of its incremental premium income in socially oriented schemes. In the case of General Insurance Corporation, the norm is 47 percent. Though these two are free to determine the avenues of investments, they are still bound by restrictions in the Insurance Act.
LIQUEFIED GAS VENTURE CLEARED

The government approved the formation of a joint venture company to import liquefied natural gas (LNG) and the construction of LNG import terminals. The joint venture company will have an authorised capital of 12 billion rupees. Four government-owned companies will collectively hold a 50 percent equity stake in the joint venture. The long term aim of this venture will be to facilitate the establishment of an LNG chain -- beginning with production at the gas fields and encompassing all other stages including liquefaction of gas, shipping, regassification and distribution for end uses. The joint venture will own only the LNG import terminals.
TELCO PIPS RELIANCE, LEVER TO TOP SLOT

The Tata group's automobiles major Telco emerged as the country's largest private sector corporation with gross sales of over 100 billion rupees in 1996/97 (April-March). Reliance Industries recorded gross sales of 90.2 billion rupees, Hindustan Lever posted sales of 71.2 billion rupees. Calculated net of excise su,rmy, Telco would still out-rank the other two companies as Reliance has inter-divisional sales of over 20 billion rupees to be deducted from its gross sales. However, Reliance continues to hold the top slot in terms of net profit, having notched up 13.23 billion rupees in 1996/97. Telco recorded a net profit of 7.62 billion rupees.
COAL INDIA PLANS EQUITY RECAST IN ALL SUBSIDIARIES

Coal India Ltd (CIL) has decided to restructure the equity capital base of all its eight subsidiaries by converting a portion of their debt into equity. CIL has already worked out the modalities. The completion of the formalities is expected to take two to three months. CIL has also drawn up a plan to invest 24.63 billion rupees in three of its loss-making subsidiaries over the next five years as part of a revival package. The equity restructuring process will be initiated at its subsidiaries, Eastern Coalfields and Bharat Coking, which have been incurring losses for the past five years. Debt-swapping will be implemented in the other six subsidiaries subsequently.
TYRE-MAKERS SKID ON MOVE TO EASE IMPORT CURBS

Domestic tyre makers fear massive dumping by foreign tyre giants, as the government prepares to lift all quantitative restrictions on the import of several consumer goods, including tyres. The companies have made a strong pitch against the government's decision to place tyres on the open general licence list, aimed at freeing imports of the listed items into the Indian market. Relaxation of the import barriers on tyres is expected to hit all domestic tyre makers.
The Observer
ICICI RETAINS GREENSHOE OPTION

ICICI has decided to retain eight billion rupees of the public issue of its unsecured redeemable bonds aggregating 7.5 billion rupees. The public issue of the bonds was oversubscribed. Against an offer of 7.5 billion rupees it received a subscription of over 22 billion rupees.
